persona_summary: BA Junior, dual concentration Finance + BAT, Econ minor, 37 courses, Good standing
question: My schedule is so tight with dual concentrations and a minor. I want to request an overload for next semester — can I take 7 courses? What should my schedule look like?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Overload requests typically require meeting a minimum GPA threshold (e.g., 3.5+) and advisor approval. The student assumes overload is just a matter of requesting it. If their GPA is below the threshold, the request would be denied.
naive_system_response: A naive system builds a 7-course schedule and says 'you'll need to request an overload approval.' It doesn't check whether the student meets the GPA requirement for overload or what the approval process entails.
correct_response: Overload requests at CMU-Q require a minimum GPA of [X] and advisor approval. Your current GPA is [check]. If you meet the threshold, here's a potential 7-course schedule: [plan]. However, I'd recommend considering whether [alternative plan with 5-6 courses + summer] might be less risky. If you don't meet the GPA threshold, overload won't be approved and you'll need to: [alternative plan].
why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent checks the overload GPA threshold before the Planning Agent builds a schedule. A single agent might build the 7-course plan first and mention the overload policy as an afterthought, or not at all.
key_facts: 7 courses is well above normal load
Alternative approaches (summer courses, adjusted sequencing) may be safer
known_traps: Building an overload schedule without checking GPA eligibility
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact overload policy including GPA threshold, (2) P-025's GPA or standing, (3) maximum units allowed in overload, (4) approval process
